title: remote.yml runs for every file its suites load, AppImage update restarts, and Windows SSH to a real Linux kernel on CI
owns: .github/workflows/remote.yml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/**, app/main/packaging or updater code for the restart, test/integration/ssh-windows.test.ts

items.title: remote.yml's new paths filter leaves out files the SSH, WSL and commands suites import at run time, so a PR to main that changes only those files runs none of those suites
items.scenario: #38 put remote.yml on pull_request and push to main, filtered by paths. The commands, SSH and WSL integration suites (commands-flow-local, commands-local, remote-ssh, remote-e2e, ssh-transport, wsl) run only in remote.yml, because ci.yml's test:integration never sets EMBER_COMMANDS_TEST or EMBER_SSH_TEST. Example: a PR that changes only app/main/policy/policy.ts. PolicyEngine is a runtime import of targets/runtime.ts:41 and remote/remote-policy.ts:13, and isSecurityWindow of wsl/privacy.ts:14. That PR runs no remote.yml job at all and merges with the remote suites unrun. The same holds for app/main/policy/target-rules.ts (wsl/privacy.ts:15), app/main/policy/remote-surface.ts (wsl/rail.ts:12), app/main/settings.ts (targets/runtime.ts:49), app/main/hands/system.ts and hands/terminals.ts (remote-apps.ts, wsl/apps.ts) and app/main/environment.ts. The filter also now applies to pushes to ember-improve/20261022-sshwsl-*, which before 63b88cd ran every suite on every push.
items.evidence: An esbuild metafile closure of the four remote suites over the merged tree (scratchpad/xreview/ship/closure/closure.mjs) lists sources outside the paths list: app/main/policy/{policy,target-rules,remote-surface,vocabulary}.ts, app/main/settings.ts, app/main/environment.ts, app/main/agent/confirm.ts, app/main/hands/{borrow,keymap,system,terminals}.ts, app/main/perception/elements.ts and app/main/platform/**. The grep of runtime imports (not `import type`) confirms the lines above. This release alone has 31 commits on policy.ts, target-rules.ts and settings.ts.
items.fix: Add app/main/policy/**, app/main/settings.ts, app/main/environment.ts, app/main/hands/**, app/main/agent/confirm.ts, app/main/perception/elements.ts and app/main/platform/** to both paths lists. Or, more robust, drop the paths filter for pull_request and main and keep it only for the sshwsl-* branches. A unit check could compare the suites' esbuild closure with the list.
items.skeptic:
I could not refute the scenario: it is real. The finding overstates how much it matters, though.

What I confirmed in /home/user/wt/relfix-int:
- Commit 7daa539 (fix/packaging, #38) added pull_request and push-to-main triggers to .github/workflows/remote.yml. Both use the same paths list (lines 20-42 and 44-66). It also added tags v*, and GitHub does not check paths for tag pushes.
- ci.yml:62 runs `npm run test:integration` with only EMBER_VOICE_TEST set. Without their variables, commands-flow-local, commands-local, ssh-transport, remote-ssh, remote-e2e and wsl all skip. So these suites run only in remote.yml.
- The runtime imports are as stated: targets/runtime.ts:41 (PolicyEngine) and :49 (settings), remote/remote-policy.ts:13, wsl/privacy.ts:14-15, wsl/rail.ts:12. Some of these files are even imported straight from the test files: commands-flow-local.test.ts:27 imports agent/confirm.ts and :34 imports settings.ts, and commands-local.test.ts:26-27 import app/main/platform/{darwin,win32}/system/*. None of them is in the paths list.
- I re-ran the finder's esbuild closure (scratchpad/xreview/ship/closure/closure.mjs) on the merged tree. It lists policy/{policy,target-rules,remote-surface,vocabulary}.ts, settings.ts, environment.ts, agent/{confirm,presenter}.ts, hands/*, perception/* and platform/** as outside the filter.
- So a PR, or a push to main, that changes only app/main/policy/policy.ts starts no remote.yml job. The lead-notes record the path filter suppressing a run (L200: the push that created sshwsl-release started no run).

Why it is less serious than "minor" suggests:
1. For PRs and main it is not a regression. At 63b88cd, remote.yml ran only on pushes to the sshwsl-* branches, on dispatch and on the weekly cron, so no PR or main push ran these suites at all. The merged result only adds coverage. Review #38 itself asked for a path filter, with a narrower list (app/main/{commands,remote,wsl,targets}, app/remote, scripts/package), and the package delivered more than that. The workflow header also says the scope is code that "touch[es] SSH, WSL or commands code".
2. Every v* tag runs every job with no filter. Nothing can be released without these suites running on the tagged commit. The gap only moves detection from merge time to tag time.
3. ci.yml runs `npm test` on every PR on Linux, Windows and macOS (lines 52, 351, 541). That covers all unit tests, including the SSH/WSL/commands unit files that use PolicyEngine and settings.
4. The one real regression against 63b88cd is that pushes to ember-improve/20261022-sshwsl-* are now filtered too. A single push trigger cannot have different paths per branch, so this comes with the design. The feature branches are finished. sshwsl-release is now only the lead's way to trigger remote.yml, and the lead already falls back to workflow_dispatch (lead-notes L200-202).

Verdict: the scenario is confirmed. It is a CI coverage gap, not a product defect, and its severity is polish to minor. The fix is still worth making, because the suites' own test files import files outside the filter: add policy/**, settings.ts, environment.ts, agent/confirm.ts, agent/presenter.ts, hands/**, perception/** and platform/** to both lists, or drop the filter for pull_request and main.

items.text: packaging: the restart after an update uses app.relaunch() without restartOptions. Inside an AppImage, process.execPath is the mounted squashfs path that goes away when the AppImage exits; Electron's docs say to relaunch with execPath = process.env.APPIMAGE. Fix it for AppImage (and check the RPM and Windows/macOS paths stay as they are); unit test with fakes.

CI only: the connect-and-hello test in test/integration/ssh-windows.test.ts runs in remote.yml's WSL1 job, where the remote's kernel is WSL1's emulated 4.4, so Ember correctly refuses ('Linux 4.18') and the real install, serve and hello over Win32-OpenSSH is never exercised. Add the same set-up to the WSL2 job (sshd in the distro on port 2222 with the runner's new Windows key authorised, the host key made known with accept-new as the WSL1 job does, remote parts built) and run ssh-windows.test.ts there, so Windows → a real Linux kernel is proven. Copy the WSL1 job's working steps; keep the WSL2 job's existing tests unchanged. Validate the YAML and bash -n the run blocks; you can't run it here, so say exactly what the next CI run must show.
